title: Candied Yams, Brown Butter
source: Built for Jarred - Southern candied yams, dialed back
ingredients: 4 lb sweet potatoes (garnet or jewel - what US stores label 'yams'), peeled, 1/2-inch rounds
3/4 cup dark brown sugar, packed (yes, less than most recipes - see notes)
1/4 tsp cayenne - optional, does not read as heat
2 tsp cider vinegar or lemon juice, at the very end
OPTIONAL TOPPING: 2 cups mini marshmallows, or 3/4 cup toasted chopped pecans
steps: Heat the oven to 375F. Butter a 9x13 baking dish.

Brown the butter: melt it in a small saucepan over medium and keep going 4-5 min, swirling, until the foam subsides and the milk solids go amber and smell nutty. Watch it - it goes from brown to burnt in under a minute.
Off the heat, whisk the brown sugar, maple syrup, orange juice, salt, cinnamon, nutmeg, cayenne and vanilla into the butter.
Put the sweet potato rounds in the dish, pour the syrup over, and toss with your hands until every piece is coated. Spread them out evenly.
Cover tightly with foil and bake 35-40 min, until a knife slides through with no resistance.
Uncover, baste with the syrup from the bottom of the dish, and bake another 20-25 min, basting twice more, until the syrup is thick and the edges are caramelizing.
Out of the oven, sprinkle the cider vinegar or lemon juice over the top and shake the dish. Rest 10 min - the syrup thickens a lot as it cools.
TOPPING, if using: scatter marshmallows over after step 6 and broil 1-2 min, watching the whole time. Pecans go on for the last 10 min of baking instead.
notes: DO NOT BOIL THE POTATOES FIRST. This is the single biggest mistake in candied yams. Boiling waterlogs them, dilutes the flavour, and the syrup slides off instead of clinging. They go into the dish raw and cook in the syrup. LESS SUGAR THAN YOU THINK. Most recipes call for 1 to 1 1/2 cups of brown sugar for this much potato. Sweet potatoes are already sweet; that much sugar makes a dessert you serve next to turkey. 3/4 cup plus the maple is plenty, and the dish actually tastes like sweet potato. SALT AND ACID ARE THE WHOLE TRICK. 1 1/2 tsp of salt and a splash of vinegar or lemon at the end are what separate this from the cloying version everyone pushes around their plate. Add the acid OFF the heat, at the very end - cooked in, it just disappears. BROWN THE BUTTER. Four extra minutes and it adds a nutty depth that plain melted butter cannot. The cayenne does the same job from the other direction: a quarter teaspoon across 4 lb is undetectable as heat and keeps the sweetness from going flat. COVERED THEN UNCOVERED. The foil steams them tender; the uncovered stretch reduces the syrup and caramelizes the edges. Skip the second half and you get sweet potatoes in a thin sugary puddle. CUT THEM EVEN - 1/2-inch rounds, as uniform as you can manage. Mixed thicknesses means some are mush while others are still firm. SIMPLER VERSION: skip the brown butter, orange juice, maple, vanilla and cayenne. Melted butter, brown sugar, salt and cinnamon tossed with the potatoes, same covered-then-uncovered bake. Keep the salt - it is the one thing not worth cutting. MAKE AHEAD, two ways. (1) Assemble completely through step 4, cover and refrigerate up to 2 days. Bake straight from the fridge and add 10-15 min to the covered time. (2) Bake it fully a day ahead, cool, refrigerate, then reheat covered at 325F for 25-30 min. Either way the topping goes on fresh at the end, never before storing - marshmallows weep and pecans go soft. OVEN TRAFFIC: this is happy anywhere from 350F to 375F, so it can share with a turkey resting at 325F; just add 10 min at the lower temp. It also holds well - it is better after 20 min on the counter than straight out of the oven. YAMS VS SWEET POTATOES: what US supermarkets sell as 'yams' are orange-fleshed sweet potatoes. True yams are a different, starchier tuber, usually at African or Caribbean markets, and they will not work here. Buy garnet or jewel.

title: Tortellini with Butternut Squash

1 hungry toddler: About 15 cubes roasted butternut squash, give or take - see ROASTING AHEAD in the notes
About 1/8 of an onion, roasted alongside - or a pinch of onion powder
2-3 Tbsp chicken or vegetable stock, milk or water
A chunk of Parmesan, about 1 Tbsp worth - no need to grate it, straight into the blender
Pasta water, as needed at the end
2 servings: 1/4 small onion, chopped, or 1 clove garlic
3 Tbsp grated Parmesan - optional, see notes for the dairy-free version
Salt, and a small squeeze of lemon at the end
4 servings: 1/2 small onion, chopped, or 2 cloves garlic
1/3 cup grated Parmesan - optional, see notes for the dairy-free version
Salt, and a squeeze of lemon at the end

steps: ONE HUNGRY TODDLER (about 20 tortellini): blend the roasted squash and onion with the butter, stock, nutmeg and the Parmesan until smooth - no need to grate the cheese first, a chunk goes straight in. Boil the tortellini, toss with the sauce, and thin with pasta water at the end, a splash at a time, until it coats rather than clumps. Two minutes of work if the squash is already roasted.

Heat the oven to 425F. Toss the squash with the olive oil and a good pinch of salt and spread it in a single layer on a sheet pan - crowded squash steams instead of browning. Roast until the edges are genuinely caramelized: 25-30 min for 1-inch pieces, 20-25 min for 2/3-inch cubes, flipping once around the 15-minute mark. Add the chopped onion to the pan for the last 15 min.
Boil the tortellini from frozen while the squash finishes. RESERVE 1 CUP of the pasta water before draining.

Blend the roasted squash and onion with the stock, butter, nutmeg, the Parmesan if using, and about 1/2 cup of the pasta water until completely smooth - 45 seconds, longer than feels necessary. Any texture left is what a kid will find.
Taste and salt properly, then add a small squeeze of lemon - it lifts the whole thing out of flat-and-sweet.
Toss with the drained tortellini over low heat for a minute, thinning with more pasta water a splash at a time until the sauce coats rather than clumps.
notes: ROASTING AHEAD IS THE WHOLE TRICK FOR A SMALL EATER. You cannot roast four cubes of squash well - they dry out before they caramelize, and preheating an oven for them is absurd. Roast a full tray once, cool it, and keep the roasted cubes in the fridge 4 days or frozen in a bag for a month. Then each meal is assembled fresh in about two minutes, which is what a toddler who wants it hot and fresh actually needs. The roasted squash is the make-ahead part; the blending, thinning and tossing all happen at dinner. THE BLENDER HANDLES EVEN THE SINGLE PORTION - no need to grate the Parmesan first, a chunk goes in whole and comes out smooth. A fork mash in a bowl also works if you would rather not wash the jug; roasted squash needs almost no effort either way. ROAST, DO NOT BOIL. Boiled squash tastes like baby food - watery and flat. The caramelized edges are where all the sweetness comes from, and the sweetness is the whole reason kids eat this. In a hurry, microwave it covered with 2 Tbsp water for 8 min and stir in 1 tsp of honey to make up for what you lost. ROASTING TIME IS ABOUT PIECE SIZE, NOT QUANTITY - a third of a cup and three cups take the same time. 1-inch pieces 25-30 min at 425F, 2/3-inch cubes 20-25 min, check at 18. For a small amount use a small pan or a toaster oven; a few cubes on a big hot sheet pan scorch at the edges before the centres soften. If the edges are browning but the centres are still firm, drop to 375F for another 5-8 min. FOR A YOUNG KID, cook past fork-tender to genuinely mashable - it should squash with light pressure between your fingers. Firm cubes are a choking risk, and a toddler rejects a texture before she ever gets to the flavour. PASTA WATER AT THE END, AS NEEDED - not a measured amount. Add it a splash at a time once the sauce and pasta are together, until it coats instead of clumping. Use pasta water rather than more stock: the starch is what makes it cling instead of sliding off into a puddle. Reserve it before you drain - everyone forgets. DAIRY-FREE / NO CHEESE: skip the Parmesan and use 1-2 Tbsp nutritional yeast (closest to a cheesy flavour), or 1 tsp white miso or 1/2 tsp soy sauce for the savoury edge. Keep the butter, or swap it for olive oil plus 1 Tbsp tahini. Then salt it properly - most 'tastes flat without cheese' is actually under-salting. WHAT ELSE CAN GO IN: roasted carrot or sweet potato (more sweetness, same colour); cauliflower, roasted on the same pan (disappears completely); a jarred roasted red pepper blended in at the end (deeper, slightly smoky). Spinach or peas work but turn the sauce green instead of orange - fine if your kids do not care about colour, a dealbreaker if they do. FOR THE ADULTS: brown a tablespoon of butter with a few sage leaves and spoon it over the top, plus black pepper and chilli flakes. Keeps the kids' bowls plain. FREEZES WELL - the sauce on its own, not with the pasta in it. Roast a whole bag of squash, make a double batch of sauce and freeze half in a jar; it is a 10-minute dinner later. Thin with water when reheating, it sets up thick in the fridge.

title: Broccoli, Butternut Squash & Lentils (No Cheese)
servings: 1 hungry toddler / about 6 kid portions - use the toggle
source: Variation on Tiny Tums Recipes (@tinytumsrecipes), de-cheesed
steps: ONE HUNGRY TODDLER: small saucepan, low heat, stir often - a shallow pan of liquid scorches fast. Oil, garlic and grated squash 2 min; add the red lentils and 1 1/4 cups stock; simmer about 13 min; add the broccoli for the last 5; top up with a splash of water any time the bottom looks dry. Off the heat, stir in the butter and the nutritional yeast or miso, then mash. About 22 minutes, all of it fresh. That is roughly a third of the full batch.
Rinse the lentils and pick out any small stones or shriveled ones.

Heat the oil in a pot over medium. Add the garlic and squash and saute 3-4 min, until the squash softens and the garlic is fragrant. GRATED CARROT and DICED SWEET POTATO go in here too, with the squash.
Add the lentils and all the stock. Bring to a boil, then simmer 18-20 min.

Add the broccoli and simmer 8-10 min more, stirring now and then, until the lentils and broccoli are very soft - 25-30 min total for the lentils. CHOPPED CAULIFLOWER goes in here, with the broccoli. Add a splash of water if it dries out.

Take it off the heat. Stir in the butter, then the nutritional yeast, miso, soy sauce or tahini. CHOPPED ROASTED RED PEPPER goes in now, off the heat - it is already cooked and simmering it just turns it to mush.
Mash with a fork to the texture she likes, loose or smooth. Taste it yourself before serving.
notes: FOR ONE TODDLER PORTION, USE RED LENTILS even though the full batch uses brown. Brown lentils need 25-30 minutes and a small pan of them will catch and burn before they soften. Red lentils collapse in about 12 minutes and are far more forgiving at this size. Lowest heat, stir often, and keep a cup of water next to the stove to top up. MAKE-AHEAD THAT STILL EATS FRESH: grate a cup of squash and chop the broccoli fine at the weekend and keep them in the fridge in separate tubs. Then a single fresh portion is a 20-minute pot with no prep, rather than a batch you reheat all week. NO CHEESE. The cheddar was doing four jobs and each has a replacement. FAT - the tablespoon of butter or oil stirred in off the heat; this is the one not to skip, it is what keeps it from tasting lean and watery. UMAMI - 1-2 Tbsp nutritional yeast is the closest thing to a cheesy flavour and has no salt, which matters under 2; 1 tsp white miso or 1/2 tsp soy sauce both work and are more savoury than cheesy; 1 Tbsp tahini gives richness and a little nuttiness. BODY - the lentils already do this, which is why this recipe misses the cheese far less than the orzo version does. SALT - for an older kid or an adult bowl, salt it at the end; most 'tastes flat without cheese' is actually under-salting. Miso, soy and tahini all bring salt, so for under 1 use the nutritional yeast or none of them. WHEN EACH ADD-IN GOES IN - this is the part that matters. GRATED CARROT and FINELY DICED SWEET POTATO go in at the start with the squash; they need the full cook, add sweetness, and keep the orange colour. FINELY CHOPPED CAULIFLOWER goes in with the broccoli for the last 8-10 min; it disappears completely into the mash and is the most invisible vegetable of the four. JARRED ROASTED RED PEPPER goes in at the very end, off the heat - it is already cooked, it only needs to warm through, and simmering it turns it to slurry. It is the biggest flavour change of the four: deeper and slightly smoky. ROASTED CARROT instead of grated is better still if the oven is already on - roast it alongside anything else and stir it in at the end. Keep add-ins to about 1 cup total or you throw off the lentil-to-liquid ratio and it goes soupy; add a splash more stock if you go heavier. AVOID SPINACH AND PEAS unless you do not mind the colour - they turn the whole thing muddy green instead of orange. LENTILS: brown lentils hold a little shape, which is fine if you are mashing. Red lentils collapse completely in about 15 min for a smoother, more sauce-like result - cut the stock to about 500 ml and the simmer to 15 min if you use them. MASHABLE SOFT is the bar for a toddler, not fork-tender; the lentils, broccoli and squash should all squash with light pressure. Lentils are high in fibre, so start with smaller portions. The squash is sauteed first for flavour and melts into the lentils; the broccoli goes in last so it stays green and does not turn sulfury. Pre-cut squash saves the peeling. FREEZE single portions in ice-cube trays and reheat with a splash of water.

1 hungry toddler: 1/4 cup dry RED lentils (about 50 g) - red, not brown, at this size; see notes
1 1/4 cups low-salt chicken or vegetable stock, plus a splash more if it dries out
1/3 cup broccoli florets, chopped very fine (pea-sized)
2 tsp butter or olive oil, stirred in at the end
INSTEAD OF THE CHEESE: 2 tsp nutritional yeast, or 1/2 tsp white miso
ADD-IN, about 1/3 cup: grated carrot; finely diced sweet potato; finely chopped cauliflower; or chopped jarred roasted red pepper
Full batch (about 6 kid portions): 150 g dry brown lentils (3/4 cup) - or red lentils, see notes
600 ml low-salt chicken or vegetable stock (about 2 1/2 cups)
1 cup butternut squash, peeled and finely grated (or diced very small)
1 cup broccoli florets, chopped very fine (pea-sized)
1 Tbsp butter or olive oil, stirred in at the end - replaces the fat the cheese was bringing
INSTEAD OF THE CHEESE, pick one: 1-2 Tbsp nutritional yeast, or 1 tsp white (shiro) miso, or 1/2 tsp soy sauce, or 1 Tbsp tahini
ADD-INS, pick one or two, about 1 cup total: grated carrot; finely diced sweet potato; finely chopped cauliflower; 1 jarred roasted red pepper, chopped

title: Cheesy Carrot & Zucchini Orzo
servings: 1 hungry toddler / about 4 kid portions - use the toggle

1 hungry toddler: 2/3 cup low-salt chicken or vegetable stock (160 ml), plus a splash more if needed
Full batch (about 4 kid portions): 450 ml low-salt chicken or vegetable stock (scant 2 cups)

steps: ONE HUNGRY TODDLER: same method, small pan, low simmer, stir every 30 seconds or so. Oil, garlic and grated veg 2 min; add the orzo and stock; 9-10 min, topping up with a splash of water whenever the bottom looks dry; cheese off the heat. About 13 minutes, all fresh. Roughly a quarter of the full batch.
Heat the oil or butter in a pan over medium-high. Add the garlic, grated carrot and grated zucchini and fry 2-3 min, until soft and fragrant.
Add the orzo and the stock. Stir and bring to a boil.
Turn down to medium and cook 10 min, stirring occasionally so it does not catch on the bottom.
When the orzo is soft, take it off the heat and stir through the grated cheddar. Serve.
notes: THE SINGLE PORTION IS THE EASIEST OF THE KID MEALS TO MAKE FRESH - 12 minutes, one small pan, no oven, nothing to prep ahead. Grate the carrot and zucchini on the fine side of the box grater straight into the pan. The only thing that changes at this size is attention: a small pan of stock goes from simmering to scorched fast, so use the smallest pan you have, the lowest heat that still bubbles, and stir constantly. Keep water next to the stove and splash it in whenever the bottom looks dry - it is almost impossible to add too much, you just cook a minute longer. The recipe is from a UK baby/toddler account - courgette is zucchini, and it is written as a weaning recipe, suitable from 6 months. THE STOCK IS THE POINT: the tight stock-to-orzo ratio is on purpose, so the orzo absorbs almost all of it and goes creamy like a risotto rather than being boiled and drained. CHEESE OFF THE HEAT, always - cheddar stirred into a boiling pan goes stringy and oily. LOW-SALT STOCK matters for a toddler; regular stock is far too salty. For adults it will taste underseasoned - salt your own bowl at the table rather than the pan. STORING (her numbers): fridge up to 4 days, freezer up to 3 months. It thickens hard as it cools, so loosen with a splash of water or stock when reheating. Grate the veg finely, not coarsely - fine grating is what makes it disappear into the sauce, which is the whole trick with kids.

title: Arroz con Gandules (Mom's)
ingredients: Olive oil, enough to cover the bottom of the caldero
2 packets Sazón Goya con Culantro y Achiote
3 cans green gandules (pigeon peas), with their liquid
Optional: 1/2 cup chopped ham or 2-3 slices bacon, browned first
steps: If using ham or bacon, brown it in the caldero first.
Cover the bottom of the caldero with olive oil and heat it. Add the sofrito and cook until fragrant.
Stir in the Sabor a Jamón, the Sazón, the gandules with their liquid and the tomato sauce. Add the water and season with salt and pepper. Bring to a boil.
Stir in the rice. Cook on medium heat until the water is absorbed.
Turn the heat to low. Cover the caldero with aluminum foil, then the lid. Cook 20-25 min without lifting the lid.
Gently fold the rice from the bottom up. Cover again with foil and the lid.
If the rice is still hard, sprinkle on 1/4-1/2 cup water and cook 10-15 min more. Scrape up the crispy pegao from the bottom and serve it too.
notes: Mom's recipe, sized for 3 cans of gandules. Her note doesn't list water; about 1 cup per cup of rice, on top of the can liquid, is an estimate. For a bigger crowd, keep 3 cans but use 6 cups rice, 3 sofrito, 3 Sabor a Jamón, 3 Sazón, about 1 can tomato sauce and about 6 cups water (about 18 cups cooked), and use the longer cook times. Lower the heat before covering so the bottom doesn't scorch. Fold gently so it doesn't get mushy.

title: Sausage & Apple Cornbread Stuffing (Mom's)
source: Arnold Cornbread Cubed Stuffing bag, doubled, with sausage and apple
ingredients: 2 bags (12 oz each) Arnold Cornbread Cubed Stuffing
2 packs sausage (6 links each), casings removed
4-8 Tbsp butter (use less if you keep some sausage fat)
steps: Heat the oven to 350F. Spray two 9x13 baking dishes.
Brown the sausage in a large skillet, breaking it into crumbles. Drain most of the fat and set the sausage aside.
Melt the butter in the same skillet over medium heat. Add the onion, celery and apple; cook 5 min.
Add the broth and whisk in the applesauce. Bring to a boil.
Put the stuffing cubes and sausage in a large bowl. Pour the hot broth mixture over, mix well and fluff with a fork.
Spread into the two dishes. Cover with foil and bake 20 min. Uncover and bake about 10 min more, until the top is lightly browned and crisp.
notes: Bag recipe doubled: the bag calls for 4 Tbsp butter, 1 cup onion, 1 cup celery and 2 cups broth per bag. Broth is cut by 1/2 cup total because the applesauce adds liquid. If it looks dry before baking, add broth a splash at a time.

title: Yam Puff (Mom's)
ingredients: About 6 lb sweet potatoes (6 cups cooked, mashed)
Up to 2 cups granulated sugar (we use a little more than 1 cup)
Butter or cooking spray for the pans
Topping: see back of card (to add)
steps: Roast the sweet potatoes whole at 400F for 45-60 min, until very soft. Cool slightly, peel, and mash. Measure 6 cups.
Mix the yams, sugar, melted butter, milk, salt, vanilla and eggs. Beat until fluffy.
Pour into 2 buttered (or sprayed) 9x12 pans, or one deep casserole dish.

Add topping, then bake UNCOVERED at 350F: 30-40 min in 9x12 pans, about 45-60 min in a deep dish, until puffed and a knife in the center comes out clean (no jiggle in the middle). If the top browns too fast, lay foil loosely over it; don't use a lid.
notes: Bake uncovered: the eggs need dry heat to puff and set; a lid traps steam and leaves it wet and flat. You can use less sugar: the doubled card amount is 2 cups, we use a little more than 1 cup. Card says 'bake as directed'; the times are estimates until the back of the card is checked. Topping is on the back of the card and still needs to be added. Make ahead: freeze the yam mixture without topping; thaw, then add topping and bake. Roast the yams rather than boil them so the puff isn't watery.

title: Red Small Kidney Beans & White Rice (Mom's)
ingredients: Sofrito (about 1/4-1/3 cup per can of beans)
1 packet Sazón Goya con Culantro y Achiote (coriander & annatto)
1 can small red kidney beans, with liquid
1 bean-can of water (a little more if needed)
steps: BEANS: Add the olive oil to the pot. Add the sofrito and cook 10 min on medium. Do not burn the sofrito.
Add the Sabor a Jamón and the Sazón.
Add the beans, then the 1/2 can tomato sauce, then 1 can of water (use the empty bean can; a little more if needed).
Simmer uncovered about 15-20 min, until the sauce thickens; mash a few beans against the pot to help. Taste for salt at the end.
RICE: Wash the rice in cold water and drain. Pour it into a pot and add cold water a little above the rice line (about 1/2 inch, the first knuckle).
Add about 1 big spoon olive oil and mix with the rice.
Bring to a boil on medium-high. Once boiling, lower to low, cover, and cook until all the water is absorbed.
Serve the beans over the rice.
notes: One of Jarred's favorite things his mom made. Her card doesn't list the sofrito amount, the bean simmer time, salt, or how much rice; those are filled in as estimates. Sazon and Sabor a Jamon are already salty, so taste before adding salt. For 15 people: 3-4 cans of beans, scaling everything else to match.
